newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa oil industry hopes for margin rise in Nov.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa oil industry hopes for margin rise in Nov.

text.p: South African oil companies hope to be awarded in November a long-awaited wholesale margin increase of three cents a litre.
"We are cautiously optimistic that we will get it in November," South African Petroleum Industry Association director Colin McClelland told Reuters on Friday.
In its monthly adjustment of petrol prices, the Central Energy Fund on Friday announced that gasoline prices would rise by one cent per litre and diesel by six cents from October 2.
But, once again, this reflected trends in international prices rather than the government meeting its commitment to ensuring that oil companies have a reasonable return on assets.
In terms of regulations, return on assets should be 15 percent but this has been steadily eroded since the last wholesale margin increase in September 1993 and was at about eight percent in 1995.

The industry had expected a wholesale margin increase by mid-1996, but a change in Mineral and Energy Affairs minister when the National Party left the government of national unity at the end of June is understood to have delayed any decision.
"They should have had an increase by now but obviously the new minister (Penuell Maduna) has had to have time to settle in and evaluate the situation himself," an analyst told Reuters.

He said that, as was expected to be shown in Engen's results for the year ended August 31 due end October, oil companies had benefited from better refining margins this year because of the weaker rand.
"But this is no excuse not to increase the wholesale margin," the analyst said. "The two operations are regarded as totally separate and should each operate profitably."
Sources said that delaying an increase in the wholesale margin could have been due to the steep increases in fuel prices earlier this year because of the weak rand.
Gasoline prices jumped 35 cents per litre between April and June while diesel prices rose 15 cents per litre.
The increases were hugely unpopular with the public and it was not seen as politically expedient to increase prices further then merely to improve the bottom lie of the oil companies.
Since July, gasoline prices have fallen 12 cents per litre and diesel prices fell five cents per litre before rising two cents per litre in September.
"We believe that there is now scope to grant the wholesale margin increase of three cents that we have asked for," McClelland said.
